Talks to the UU Remote main application over XPC; intended for AI agents and automation scripts.

Human-readable text by default; append --json for stable JSON output, which scripts must use.
Success goes to stdout; usage errors, connection failures and business failures go to stderr with a non-zero exit code.
Device, cloud PC and session operations take the resource ID as TARGET - run the matching list command first.

EXAMPLES:
  uuyc-cli --version                    # Print the CLI version only
  uuyc-cli version --json               # CLI, app version and build
  uuyc-cli status                       # System status and diagnostics
  uuyc-cli echo ping                    # Test main app communication
  uuyc-cli user info                    # Current signed-in user
  uuyc-cli user wallet                  # Wallet balance
  uuyc-cli device list                  # Device list with online state
  uuyc-cli device connect TARGET        # Connect to a device by ID
  uuyc-cli device disconnect            # Disconnect every device
  uuyc-cli device status                # Device connection status
  uuyc-cli cloudpc list                 # Cloud PC list
  uuyc-cli cloudpc launch TARGET        # Power on a cloud PC by ID
  uuyc-cli cloudpc connect TARGET       # Connect to a cloud PC by ID
  uuyc-cli assist id                    # This device's remote assist ID
  uuyc-cli assist allow on              # Allow remote assist
  uuyc-cli term -d TARGET list          # Remote terminal sessions
  uuyc-cli term -d TARGET new NAME      # Create and open a session
  uuyc-cli lterm list                   # Local UU terminal sessions

Manage remote terminal sessions on a controlled device.

Sessions are addressed by device ID plus session name; internal session IDs are never
exposed. -d/--device may appear before or after the subcommand.

SUBCOMMANDS:
  new        Create a session and open its terminal window in the main application
  attach     Open an existing session in a terminal window
  ls, list   List terminal sessions
  has        Check whether a session exists (exit code 0 exists, 1 missing)
  rename     Rename a session
  kill       Terminate a session

EXAMPLES:
  uuyc-cli term -d dev-001 new                      Create a session
  uuyc-cli term -d dev-001 new NAME                 Create a named session
  uuyc-cli term -d dev-001 new NAME --shell cmd
                                                    Create with explicit shell
  uuyc-cli term -d dev-001 attach                   Open the only session
  uuyc-cli term -d dev-001 attach NAME              Open a named session
  uuyc-cli term -d dev-001 list                     List sessions
  uuyc-cli term -d dev-001 list --json              List sessions as JSON
  uuyc-cli term -d dev-001 has NAME                 Check session exists
  uuyc-cli term -d dev-001 rename OLD NEW           Rename a session
  uuyc-cli term -d dev-001 kill NAME                Terminate a session

Manage local UU Remote terminal sessions on this machine.

Sessions are addressed by session name; internal session IDs are never
exposed. new and attach take over the current terminal and require a TTY.

SUBCOMMANDS:
  new        Create a session and attach it in the current terminal (no --json)
  attach     Attach an existing session in the current terminal (no --json)
  ls, list   List terminal sessions
  has        Check whether a session exists (exit code 0 exists, 1 missing)
  rename     Rename a session
  kill       Terminate a session

EXAMPLES:
  uuyc-cli lterm new NAME                  Create and attach
  uuyc-cli lterm new NAME --shell bash     Create with bash shell
  uuyc-cli lterm attach                    Attach the only session
  uuyc-cli lterm attach NAME               Attach a named session
  uuyc-cli lterm list                      List sessions
  uuyc-cli lterm list --json               List sessions as JSON
  uuyc-cli lterm has NAME                  Check session exists
  uuyc-cli lterm rename OLD NEW            Rename a session
  uuyc-cli lterm kill NAME                 Terminate a session

limitations: The session serves operations only after Ghidra reports default auto-analysis complete; incomplete analysis does not expose partial results.
The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.

Only Ghidra-defined string Data is observed; packed or undefined string bytes may be absent. Completeness applies to that inventory, and an empty search does not establish that text is absent from the artifact. If an address is known, use read_bytes and xrefs to inspect bytes and references.

Regex mode uses Java Pattern semantics. Matcher or compiler stack exhaustion returns a resource constraint without closing the session; literal mode avoids regex recursion and returns complete matching values.
